decisions.evidence: The first exponent contains a d-like loop and stem, but the stem is densely retraced and has additional high angular strokes. Its entire form cannot be resolved as an unaltered letter, and no earlier sign is identified.

The middle exponent has an exposed lower d-like loop, with a tall angular upper stem/overwriting stroke. The additional high stroke keeps the reading tentative. The whole formula, including its indices and separator, was inspected.

The right exponent has a d-like lower loop and a separate terminal 1. A short horizontal stroke abuts the heavy tall stem; a complete separate plus is not exposed clearly enough to exclude the d1 alternative.
The crop shows p, compressed ri, a clear low v, and accented é. The two raised end marks serve as quotation strokes; there is no tall f or c/t sequence for the C alternatives.

The whole inline formula shows one horizontal shaft with a small down tick at the right end, without the open angled pair seen on the lower array's right-directed arrow. The headless second alternative is retained.

The final superscript in the lower object is heavily retraced and crossed. Its location and arms support a star reading, but the dense angular upper stroke leaves the state of the sign unresolved; no cancellation is silently erased.

The raised correction has a low e/s sequence and a separate tall crossed final t. It has neither the initial d-loop of du nor the length and letter strokes of ensuite. This resolves the word only, not its attachment or the cancellation state of the underlying d'un.

notes: The upper display is presented as a definition and is described in the upper-right text as a quoted privé skeleton of codimension d. The three displayed exponents retain their source-based doubts. The body states that the written reference 225 induces a local isomorphism from the indicated D to the indicated Theta. It cancels an initial formulation over two baselines, then gives the central comparison and a definition of the tilded index tuple. The next display carries stars. The lower prose refers to (223), and the displayed array factors the written D expression through the middle object, with a separate vertical comparison to the lower Theta. The final prose describes a morphisme étale fini followed by an inclusion; the raised est, underlying d'un and their uncertain relationship are preserved literally, without repairing the grammar. The page ends mid-sentence after est. No assertion has been proved, disproved, normalized, or repaired mathematically in this reading. The source numeral beneath the central display's current last digit is not identified. Full scan and both prepared halves were viewed once each; all fifteen first-reading crops were inspected. No OCR, external research, or TeX compilation was used. Localized second-reading boxes have neutral spatial/category labels; neighboring baselines are contextual where the manuscript's sloping writing makes small incidental fragments enter a box.

deletion_insertion_check: The cancelled morphisme was inspected separately: its high h, descending p, dotted i and low ending survive beneath the horizontal strike; the deletion is retained. The indexed expression after sur has dense diagonal cancellation; its index d'_* is exposed while D/Theta remains doubtful. The two long cancelled baselines include the Theta expression, s'identifie, a doubtful separate à and a visible terminal colon, followed by the crossed endpoint-index expression, later tilded-index D, comma and doubtful où. The central où is live, followed by a distinct cancelled d, now read from its loop and stem. The clean tilded-index definition belongs to the following baseline. At the bottom, the raised correction reads est; C's treatment of all of d'un as deleted is not secure because the curve lies above most letter bodies, so live/cancelled alternatives are preserved and the insertion attachment is not asserted as settled. The looped lower ink beneath induit remains an additional uncertainty rather than an invented readable deletion. No underlying character has been invented under the retraced upper exponents or overwritten central formula numeral.
legibility: The live prose is generally legible, including privé and on sait. The overwritten opening exponents and the two crossed baselines remain the least secure areas. The raised est is legible but its attachment to the surrounding words and the state of d’un remain uncertain. H preserves the colon that C omits; both drafts give a terminal point absent after the second isom. Neither witness resolves the dense overwritten signs.
root_adjudication: Main reader inspected the whole scan and all fifteen saved crops. Approved the exposed word forms and punctuation. Retained the uncertainties in the exponents, lower star, crossed formula and raised correction; no mathematical repair supplied. Confirmed the rotated similarity mark beneath the middle object and the differing visible endpoints of the two upper connectors in (229).
